newsitem.title: USA: Stocks higher; Wall Street bets Fed will hold line on rates.
newsitem.headline: Stocks higher; Wall Street bets Fed will hold line on rates.

text.p: Stocks were higher in early trading Tuesday as Wall Street bet the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged.

Around 10 a.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 24.16 points at 7,827.52, building on Monday's 109-point rebound after Friday's dizzying plunge of 247 points on worries about the shape of future corporate profits.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 8.98 points at 1,578.50.
The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee convened for its sixth interest rate meeting this year at 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT) and a decision was expected at 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT).

Analysts said that, even though the consensus is that the Fed will hold the line on interest rates amid subdued inflation, they still expect the market will be on the defensive until the central bank wraps up its meeting.

"The markets are going to be somewhat on the defensive usually until we hear from the FOMC, though nobody expects them to raise rates," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Investors were also scrutinizing the tentative agreement between United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union to end their 15-day strike for its effect on future inflation and corporate earnings.

Union President Ron Carey declared victory and said the Teamsters won sweeping concessions for additional full-time jobs, better union pensions and improved pay that "sends a signal that American workers are on the move again."

In the economic news, the Commerce Department reported that housing starts in July were at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.447 million, unchanged from June when starts increased a revised 3.2 percent from May. Wall Street analysts had forecast a slightly stronger 1.46-million-unit building pace for July.
The bond market was flat with the yield on the Treasury's 30-year issue holding at Monday's close of 6.52 percent.
